report.source_text: A right mini-thoracotomy was performed through the fifth intercostal space with anticipation toward the right lower lobectomy, considering a parenchymal lesion. However, the opening of the chest cavity revealed a tubular, narrow-based pedunculated, mobile, pinkish, cystic smooth lesion arising from the mediastinum around the area of the inferior pulmonary ligament (Fig. 3). There was no adhesion with surrounding structures, and the lesion was completely mobile. The entire lesion was removed just ligating the stalk.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 12-year-old boy presented with occasional mild right-sided chest pain and a non-resolving shadow on chest X-ray. Initial chest X-ray (E001) showed a tubular inhomogeneous opacity in the medial part of the right lower lung field. A subsequent CECT chest (E002) further delineated a well-defined, thin-walled cystic lesion (8.5 × 3.6 × 4.5 cm) within the right lower lobe with mild marginal enhancement. Surgical exploration via right mini-thoracotomy (E004) revealed a tubular, narrow-based pedunculated, mobile, pinkish, cystic smooth lesion arising from the mediastinum around the inferior pulmonary ligament, which was completely removed. Histopathological examination (E005) confirmed the lesion to be a bronchogenic cyst, lined by respiratory epithelium with seromucinous gland, cartilage, and smooth muscle.
